comparisons.peer_summary: The company utilizes outsourcing to protect intellectual property and accelerate time to market for its products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom discuss manufacturing strategies aimed at accelerating time-to-market, but they employ opposite operational models. Intel emphasizes in-house proprietary manufacturing to quickly scale products, whereas Broadcom utilizes outsourcing for the same objective of accelerating time to market. Intel states, 'This enables us to optimize performance, shorten time-to-market for new product introductions, and more quickly scale products in high volume,' while Broadcom notes, 'By doing so, we can protect our IP and accelerate time to market for our products.'

comparisons.peer_topic: Global manufacturing footprint and subcontractor use
comparisons.peer_summary: Products are manufactured in own facilities across seven countries and utilize subcontractors for certain processes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose a heavy reliance on their own internal manufacturing facilities to produce their core products. Intel states, 'We manufacture a majority of our products in our own manufacturing facilities using our proprietary process technologies,' while Micron confirms, 'We manufacture our products within our own facilities located in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, China, and India and also utilize subcontractors to perform certain manufacturing processes.' Both companies highlight internal capacity as a key part of their operations.
